bearings.paper_claim: Test accuracy across all 156 speakers 0.913568 (0.914) and across 34 candidates 0.945769 (0.946); MFCC CNN 0.081 and 0.134. Per-debate wav2vec2 0.974 (+/-0.024) vs MFCC 0.888 (+/-0.085). Section 4.2 (p.319) warns that cross-speaker acoustic comparisons are confounded by microphone placement, compression and sampling. The paper does not describe its train/test split.

Only 5% of pairs rated not aligned at all, concentrated in short or interrupted sentences (Figure 2b). The paper proposes no word floor and no ASR word-match threshold.

The paper reports no effect size for the gender pattern and does not say pitch comparisons reflect speaker and voice.

bearings.paper_claim: Energy is normalized by each debate's average loudness (Section 4.2, p.319). Comparisons across speakers and time are subject to confounding by microphone placement, compression and sampling (p.319). The paper recommends normalization or comparison with baselines where possible and does not say normalization leaves residual confounding. Naive cross-speaker interpretation is cautioned (p.325). The paper's own Figure 3a ranks candidates by raw cross-speaker average pitch.
bearings.paper_location: Section 4.2 pp.319 (normalization, confound warning) and p.325 (naive interpretation); analyst cited p.324
bearings.system_side: b5_audio_build.py lines 85-104: duration-weighted means per member, z-score over all pooled members (mu and sd across members), clipped at +/-5. No loudness or channel normalization appears in b5_audio_build.py. The cache note on line 104 says z-within-source, which contradicts the pooled code. volume_dynamics_raw uses loudness stddevNorm (a mean-normalized within-clip functional), so it is partly level-invariant; the blanket statement should say so.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Applies to cross-member readings of volume dynamics, pitch level and strain. Within-member and ICC uses are less exposed. Whether pause and pace are less channel-sensitive is not tested in the paper and remains UNVERIFIED.
bearings.verifier_note: Code claim verified for the pooled z-score and absence of loudness normalization in the build file. Paper claim that normalization is insufficient is not in the text. Page cite corrected. Stale z-within-source note flagged.

related.why: Melange's topic_emotional_intensity code credits Dietrich, Hayes and O'Brien for the within-speaker deviation design (b5_audio_descriptors_candidate.py lines 209-210, verified). Mestre and Ryan cite that paper only for pitch tracking emotional state (p.316), not for the deviation design. Dietrich studies congressional speech (verified from item title).

Item exists. It is an image-only methods paper on politicians' Facebook photographs, not images and video. The shared validation and bias caution is analyst framing and was not checked against the Joo extraction.

Item exists; its title is about personalised models for self-reported personality recognition. No extraction is on file, so the prosody and sex-confound-test claims are UNVERIFIED. Mestre and Ryan do not cite it.

Item exists; its research question asks how much trait information voice features carry, which parallels the caution about inferring traits from voice. Mestre and Ryan do not cite it, so the link is analyst framing.

summary_issues: Summary says the authors call emotion models biased by gender and pitch. Paper (p.324-325) says they can encode and amplify such biases and mentions potential gender and racial bias; it reports no measured bias. Softened.

Summary says the 0.914 accuracy is confounded by microphone placement and compression. The paper's confound warning (p.319) concerns cross-speaker and cross-time acoustic comparisons, not classifier accuracy.

Summary says the paper backs the fix for the sex confound in pitch variability and cautions against pooled eGeMAPS z-scores. Neither is in the paper: it never mentions eGeMAPS or z-scores, and the sex-confound fix is Melange's own (commit 4193f0140). Refuted.

Summary says b5_audio_neural_head.py cites section 4.3 and footnote 9. That citation is in b5_audio_neural_pilot.py line 225. The head docstring names the experiment only and says the paper mean-pools; p.321 says only 768-dimensional embeddings for each sentence.
Page locations to correct: Table 3 is on p.322 not p.321; speaker-dependent validation and within-speaker shifts are on p.325 not p.324; the Dietrich pitch-emotion citation is p.316.

Paper counts to avoid quoting without denominators: 47,150 sentences (p.314) vs 44,559 sentences and 36,833 candidate sentences (p.321) vs 38,649 candidate sentences (p.314). Section 4.4 (p.325) refers to Figure 3d, which the Figure 3 caption does not contain.
